A pretty to look at point-and-click puzzler that could have been great if not for a few really unfortunate puzzle choices that frankly ruin the experience, unless you are really proficient at math.

+ Difficulty level for most of the puzzles is just right
+ Puzzle variety is satisfactory overall
+ You can save manually at any time, even mid-level, with several available slots
+ Nice array of achievements, with a few missables that are not too difficult to get

+/- Simple and humorous story
+/- Passable background music and game sounds

- While most of the puzzles are solvable, some of them require math skills that will make the game next to unplayable for the average player
- The hint system, while cute and helpful half the time, is completely useless for quite a few of the puzzles. You'll often find yourself trying to solve a difficult puzzle and the hint will be "do this in order to unlock the puzzle, and then... solve the puzzle"
- Puzzle difficulty varies wildly and is pretty uneven, meaning some puzzles in the latter part of the game can be much easier than previous ones
- One (non-math) puzzle in particular in Chapter 5 [spoiler](the square and the sliding doors)[/spoiler] almost made me quit the game. Had to turn to a guide for that one, because I wasn't prepared to spend endless hours on one particularly repetitive and un-fun puzzle. Maybe it's just me, but @#$% that puzzle

I willed myself to the end because I hate abandoning games halfway plus I'm an achievement hunter, but sadly I can't recommend this to the average puzzle lover. Which is really a shame, because if you take out the weird fixation with math problems, the game was very much enjoyable for the most part.

Mr. Pumpkin Adventure, developed and published by Cotton Game, is a surreal point-and-click puzzle adventure that leans heavily into atmosphere, visual storytelling, and unconventional logic. From the moment the game begins, players are placed in control of the titular Mr. Pumpkin, who awakens in a strange, vegetable-themed world with no memory of who he is or how he arrived there. This amnesiac premise serves as a narrative anchor, but the game quickly establishes that clarity is not its primary goal. Instead, it invites players to piece together meaning through exploration, visual cues, and abstract environmental storytelling.

The gameplay follows traditional point-and-click adventure mechanics, with static 2D scenes filled with interactive objects, hidden items, and layered puzzles. Players must carefully examine each environment, collecting tools and clues that can be combined or used in specific contexts to unlock progression. The puzzles vary in type, ranging from logic-based challenges and pattern recognition tasks to more obscure riddles that demand lateral thinking. Solutions are rarely obvious, and the game expects players to experiment and observe rather than rely on direct hints. This design philosophy can be deeply rewarding when the pieces finally fall into place, but it also means that certain puzzles may feel opaque or unintuitive, especially for those accustomed to more guided adventure games.

Visually, Mr. Pumpkin Adventure stands out for its distinctive art direction. The world is rendered in a stylized, hand-drawn aesthetic that blends whimsical charm with subtle unease. Characters are exaggerated and expressive, environments are filled with peculiar details, and nearly every screen feels like a small, self-contained illustration. The vegetable-themed inhabitants and bizarre architecture create a setting that is playful on the surface yet strangely melancholic underneath. This balance between lighthearted absurdity and quiet mystery gives the game a unique identity that lingers long after individual puzzles are solved.

The soundtrack and sound design further reinforce the atmosphere. Music shifts between gentle, almost whimsical melodies and more haunting, minimalistic compositions, enhancing the feeling that something is slightly off beneath the surface. Ambient sounds and subtle audio cues help bring the environments to life without overwhelming the player. Because dialogue is sparse and storytelling often occurs through comic-style interludes between chapters, sound and imagery carry much of the emotional weight. The narrative unfolds in fragments, leaving room for interpretation rather than delivering straightforward exposition. For some players, this ambiguity enhances the intrigue; for others, it may feel disconnected or incomplete.

Progression is divided into chapters, each introducing new environments and increasingly complex puzzle chains. As the game advances, puzzles tend to become more layered, sometimes requiring multiple steps across different screens before a solution reveals itself. This escalation keeps the experience engaging, though it can also contribute to moments of stagnation if a particular clue is overlooked. The relatively compact length of the game means it can typically be completed in a few focused sessions, making it approachable without demanding an overwhelming time investment.

One of the strengths of Mr. Pumpkin Adventure lies in how it encourages careful observation. Small visual details often contain essential hints, and environmental storytelling rewards attentive players. Rather than guiding you with explicit instructions, the game trusts you to interpret symbols, patterns, and contextual clues. This approach fosters a sense of discovery that feels personal and earned. However, because the logic occasionally borders on abstract, players who prefer clear cause-and-effect puzzle design may encounter frustration in certain sequences.

Ultimately, Mr. Pumpkin Adventure succeeds as a distinctive indie adventure that prioritizes mood, artistry, and puzzle experimentation over traditional narrative structure. It does not attempt to redefine the point-and-click genre, but it confidently embraces its surreal identity and delivers a cohesive, if enigmatic, journey. For players who appreciate unconventional storytelling, stylized visuals, and puzzles that demand patience and creative thinking, it offers a memorable and atmospheric experience. Its charm lies not in grand scope or dramatic twists, but in the quiet strangeness of its world and the satisfaction of unraveling its mysteries one careful click at a time.

В целом, довольно приятная игра, где сюжет повествуется через комиксы, а потому наличие русского языка не обязательно. Есть еще дневник персонажа, но и там вполне все понятно. 
Визуал мне понравился, изучать надписи на стенах и всякие мелочи было интересно. Загадки интуитивны и логичны. К прохождению советую.
